st: To make the rice powder, toast [[2 tbsp]] uncooked glutinous rice in a dry pan over medium heat for 5 minutes until deep golden, then grind it into a coarse powder.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and add the chicken with [[0.25 cup]] water.
Cook, breaking the meat up with a spoon, for 6 to 8 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and no pink remains.
Remove from the heat and let it cool for 5 minutes so the herbs do not wilt.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] fish sauce, [[3 tbsp]] lime juice and [[1 tsp]] chili flakes.
Mix in the shallots, green onions and the toasted rice powder.
Fold in [[0.5 cup]] mint and [[0.5 cup]] cilantro and taste, adding more lime or fish sauce if needed.
Serve warm or at room temperature with sticky rice and lettuce leaves.

ing: padaek; or use extra fish sauce
st: Peel the green papaya and shred it with a grater or julienne peeler. Soak in cold water for 10 minutes and drain well.
Pound the garlic and chilies in a large mortar with a pestle into a rough paste.
Add [[1 tsp]] sugar, [[2 tbsp]] fish sauce, [[1 tbsp]] fermented fish sauce and [[2 tbsp]] lime juice and stir.
Add the long beans and gently bruise them with the pestle.
Add the shredded papaya and pound gently while turning with a spoon, for 1 minute, until softened but still crunchy.
Add the tomatoes and press gently so they release some juice.
Taste and balance: add more lime for sour, fish sauce for salt, or sugar for sweetness.
Top with [[2 tbsp]] peanuts and serve at once with sticky rice.

ing: also called sweet or sticky rice
st: Rinse [[2 cups]] glutinous rice in a bowl of cold water, swishing and draining 3 times, until the water is mostly clear.
Cover with [[4 cups]] fresh water and soak for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Fill a pot with 2 inches of water and set a steamer basket or bamboo steamer over it. Line it with a banana leaf or damp cheesecloth.
Drain the rice well and spread it in the steamer in an even layer.
Bring the water to a boil, cover, and steam for 20 minutes.
Flip the rice over with a spatula and steam 5 to 10 more minutes until translucent and chewy.
For a sweet version, warm [[0.5 cup]] coconut milk, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt, stir into the rice and let stand 5 minutes.
Serve warm, wrapped in a cloth or lidded basket, and eat with your hands.

ing: Lao pepper wood; or use 0.5 tsp Sichuan peppercorns
st: Soak [[2 tbsp]] glutinous rice in water for 30 minutes, then grind it into a rough paste with a little water.
Pound the chilies, garlic, shallots and lemongrass into a paste.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a pot over medium heat and fry the paste for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the beef and stir for 5 minutes to brown it lightly.
Pour in [[5 cups]] water, add the sakhan wood, and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes until the beef is tender.
Stir in the rice paste and [[3 tbsp]] fish sauce and simmer for 5 minutes until thickened.
Add the eggplant and long beans and cook 10 minutes until tender.
Stir in the dill and scallions, remove the wood pieces, and serve hot with sticky rice.
Put the chicken, [[6 cloves]] smashed garlic, ginger and [[8 cups]] water in a pot. Bring to a boil and skim the foam.
Simmer gently for 40 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Remove the chicken, shred the meat, and strain the broth back into the pot.
Season the broth with [[2 tbsp]] fish sauce and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Fry [[2 cloves]] sliced garlic in [[2 tbsp]] oil over medium heat for 2 minutes until golden. Set aside.
Bring the broth to a boil, add the noodles, and cook 4 to 5 minutes until chewy and the broth thickens slightly.
Divide the noodles and broth among bowls and top with chicken, fried garlic and scallions.
Add [[0.5 cup]] cilantro, [[1 tsp]] black pepper and a squeeze of lime to each bowl.

ing: such as catfish or tilapia, chopped
st: Soften the banana leaves by dipping briefly in hot water or passing over a flame. Wipe dry.
Chop the fish into small pieces until almost a paste, and put it in a bowl.
Add the lemongrass, shallots, garlic, chilies, lime leaves, dill and scallions.
Stir in the egg, [[2 tbsp]] fish sauce and [[2 tbsp]] rice flour until sticky and well combined.
Spoon a quarter of the mixture onto the center of each leaf.
Fold the leaf over into a rectangular packet and secure the ends with toothpicks or string.
Set a steamer over boiling water and steam the packets for 25 minutes until the fish is firm and cooked through.
Open and serve warm with sticky rice.
Pound the lemongrass, garlic, shallots, galangal and chilies in a mortar or food processor into a coarse paste.
Mix the paste with the pork, lime leaves, cilantro, [[2 tbsp]] fish sauce and [[1 tsp]] salt, kneading well for 3 minutes.
Fry a small patty to taste and adjust the seasoning.
Chill the mix in the fridge for 1 hour to firm up and blend flavors.
If using casings, rinse and stuff the mixture in loosely, twisting off links. Otherwise shape into thick logs.
Prick the sausages with a pin in a few places.
Cook in a pan with [[1 tbsp]] oil over medium-low heat for 20 minutes, turning, until browned and the pork reaches 160°F (71°C).
Slice and serve with sticky rice and a chili dip.
Soak the dried chilies in hot water for 15 minutes to soften, then drain.
Heat a dry skillet over medium heat and roast the unpeeled garlic and shallots for 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until charred and soft.
Toast the galangal and chilies in the same pan for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Peel the garlic and shallots once they are cool enough to handle.
Pound everything in a mortar, or blend, to a thick, slightly coarse paste.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a small pan and fry the paste over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] fish sauce and [[1 tbsp]] sugar and simmer 3 minutes until thick and dark.
Add [[1 tbsp]] lime juice, cool, and serve with sticky rice or grilled meat. Refrigerate in a jar for up to 2 weeks.

ing: thinly sliced, cooked or Lao style ham
st: Mix [[2 tbsp]] vinegar, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt until dissolved, then soak the carrot strips for 15 minutes.
If the pork is raw, cook it in a pan until it reaches 145°F (63°C) and no longer pink, about 6 minutes.
Toss the cooked pork with [[1 tbsp]] soy sauce.
Warm the baguettes in a 350°F (175°C) oven for 5 minutes until crisp outside.
Split each loaf and spread the pate along one side and [[2 tbsp]] mayonnaise on the other.
Layer the pork, cucumber, drained pickled carrots, cilantro and chili slices.
Press the sandwich closed and cut in half if you like.
Eat right away while the bread is still crisp.
